title: Your four foundations
hookLine: a sitting that moves through body, feeling, mind and dhammas

cards: For three weeks, the Satipatthana Sutta, the discourse on the foundations of mindfulness, came one section at a time: the breath, the postures, the bag of grain, the charnel ground, the second arrow, the five visitors, the six doors, the seven factors.
Today it comes together the way it was meant to be used: not as a list, but as one sitting. Today: your four foundations.

teach.h: THE WHOLE SUTTA IN ONE BREATH.
teach.b: Here's the whole sutta in one breath. Satipatthana: one way, four doors. The refrain: ardent and gentle.
First foundation, the body. Knowing the breath, like the turner at the lathe. The chorus: it arises, it passes.
The postures: I know I'm sitting. Clear knowing: even this. The parts: a bag of grain.
The elements: four elements. The charnel ground: this body too. Second foundation, feelings: pleasant, painful, neither, and one arrow, not two.

Third foundation, the mind: know the mind, and just know it. Fourth foundation, dhammas: the hindrances, it came, it went; five heaps; the fetter at the door; seven factors; and the four truths, know it as it is.
And the promise: even seven days. It sounds like a lot.

teach.h: FROM MOST SOLID TO MOST SUBTLE.
teach.b: But one way teachers read the order is from the most solid to the most subtle.

teach.h: ONE IS ALWAYS UNDER YOUR FEET.
teach.b: The body is easy to find: you can always feel your seat. Feelings are quicker, a flicker of pleasant or painful. The mind is subtler again, its whole weather.
And dhammas are the patterns running through all of it.
Each one is a place to stand. On a scattered day, you might only manage the first. On a clear day, you might move through all four.
In another sutta, the Buddha calls the four a person's own home ground: a quail caught by a hawk out in the open field is safe again among the clods of its own ploughed field.
The practice isn't to master all four at once. It's to know that wherever you are, one of them is right under your feet.

how: Many practitioners do a sitting that moves through body, feelings, mind and dhammas in turn, and on retreats in the Theravada and insight traditions all four are practiced throughout the day, in sitting, walking and daily tasks.

o: a breathing method for calming the body before sleep
a Pali chant recited each morning to protect a home
the foundations of mindfulness: body, feelings, mind, dhammas

games.q: match each foundation to one of its lines.

s: the four foundations move from most subtle to most solid
they move from most solid, the body, to most subtle, the dhammas.
the practice is to master all four at once
it's to know that one of them is always under your feet.
the body is often the easiest place to start
you can always feel your seat and your breath.

games.q: it's a scattered, busy day and you have one minute. which foundation is the easiest place to stand?
o: the body: feel your feet, your seat, your breath.
the dhammas: analyze the five heaps.
none: wait for a calmer day.
games.why: the body is the most solid of the four and always available. on a scattered day, it's enough.

practice: Take about thirty seconds for each foundation: the body, the breath and the shape of your posture; feelings, what's pleasant, unpleasant or neither; the mind, tight or open, scattered or gathered; dhammas, a hindrance here, or a factor of awakening, a little calm, a little curiosity.
Then rest wherever you find yourself. The full version runs fifteen minutes, for any quiet morning you have.

wordCard.voice: Satipatthana, the foundations of mindfulness: one way and four doors, covering the body, feelings, the mind and dhammas, held together in a single sitting.

orig.note: Pali satipaṭṭhāna: the foundations, or establishing, of mindfulness.

carryVoice: Your line: four places to stand. Tomorrow a new part begins: the Heart Sutra. Three weeks in one sutta, done.
